content.text:
You are checking a netlist that an automatic computer-vision pipeline extracted from an analog circuit schematic. Your job is to find and fix its mistakes.

You are given two images:
  IMAGE 1: the original schematic. This is the ground truth - trust it over everything else.
  IMAGE 2: the same schematic annotated by the pipeline (enlarged x2.00):
    - grey boxes with IDs (M1, R2, ...) = detected components;
    - letters next to black dots = the pin the pipeline assigned to that lead
      (MOSFET D/G/S/B, BJT C/B/E, op-amp +/-/out, o+/o- for differential outputs,
      sources +/- or in/out, two-terminal parts 1 = Pos, 2 = Neg);
    - wires are coloured by net, and each net has a name tag in its colour;
      the SAME colour means the pipeline thinks the wires are connected;
    - red "?" dot = a line touching a component that was not assigned to any pin;
    - red box "J" = crossing treated as NOT connected; green box "X" = crossing treated as connected.
  The annotation can be wrong. Check every suspicious spot against IMAGE 1.

Pipeline netlist (component ID, type, pin -> net). GND and VDD come from ground / supply
symbols; netK are the other nets; ncK means the pin was left unconnected:
  M1   PMOS      Drain=net1, Gate=net1, Source=VDD, Body=net2
  M2   PMOS      Drain=net1, Gate=net1, Source=VDD
  M3   PMOS      Drain=net3, Gate=net1, Source=VDD
  M4   PMOS      Drain=net4, Gate=net4, Source=net1, Body=net5
  M5   PMOS      Drain=net6, Gate=net7, Source=net8, Body=net1
  M6   PMOS      Drain=net9, Gate=net10, Source=net1, Body=net11
  M7   PMOS      Drain=nc1, Gate=nc2, Source=nc3
  M8   PMOS      Drain=net12, Gate=net4, Source=net9
  M9   PMOS      Drain=net4, Gate=net4, Source=net13
  C1   Cap       Pos=net14, Neg=net12
  R1   Res       Pos=net12, Neg=net12
  M10  NMOS      Drain=net15, Gate=net15, Source=net16
  M11  NMOS      Drain=net4, Gate=net15, Source=net16
  M12  NMOS      Drain=net3, Gate=net12, Source=net16
  M13  NMOS      Drain=net4, Gate=net4, Source=net17
  M14  NMOS      Drain=net12, Gate=net4, Source=net18
  R2   Res       Pos=net17, Neg=net16
  R3   Res       Pos=net18, Neg=net16

Crossings:
  (none detected)

Spots where the pipeline itself was unsure:
  - M1.Body: attached through a very small blob, maybe text rather than a wire (net2).
  - M4.Body: attached through a very small blob, maybe text rather than a wire (net5).
  - M5.Source: attached through a very small blob, maybe text rather than a wire (net8).
  - M6.Body: attached through a very small blob, maybe text rather than a wire (net11).
  - M7: detected as PMOS with low confidence (0.36).
  - M7.Drain: no wire found at this lead (left unconnected as nc1).
  - M7.Gate: no wire found at this lead (left unconnected as nc2).
  - M7.Source: no wire found at this lead (left unconnected as nc3).
  - M7: 2 extra line(s) touch the box but were not assigned to any pin (red '?' marks).
  - M8.Gate: attached through a very small blob, maybe text rather than a wire (net4).
  - C1: 1 extra line(s) touch the box but were not assigned to any pin (red '?' marks).
  - R1: 1 extra line(s) touch the box but were not assigned to any pin (red '?' marks).
  - M12: detected as NMOS with low confidence (0.39).
  - M14: detected as NMOS with low confidence (0.47).
  - net11: only one pin (M6.Body) and no input/output port - a dangling wire, or it should join another net.
  - net13: only one pin (M9.Source) and no input/output port - a dangling wire, or it should join another net.
  - net14: only one pin (C1.Pos) and no input/output port - a dangling wire, or it should join another net.
  - net2: only one pin (M1.Body) and no input/output port - a dangling wire, or it should join another net.
  - net5: only one pin (M4.Body) and no input/output port - a dangling wire, or it should join another net.
  - net6: only one pin (M5.Drain) and no input/output port - a dangling wire, or it should join another net.
  - net8: only one pin (M5.Source) and no input/output port - a dangling wire, or it should join another net.

Allowed component types and their pins:
  NMOS: Drain, Source, Gate, Body  (Body optional)
  PMOS: Drain, Source, Gate, Body  (Body optional)
  NPN: Base, Emitter, Collector
  PNP: Base, Emitter, Collector
  Res: Pos, Neg
  Cap: Pos, Neg
  Ind: Pos, Neg
  Diode: In, Out
  Voltage: Positive, Negative
  Current: In, Out
  Diso_amp: InN, InP, Out
  Siso_amp: In, Out
  Dido_amp: InN, InP, OutN, OutP

Typical pipeline errors to look for:
- a wire attached to the wrong pin, or a MOSFET drain and source swapped;
- two different nets merged (text, arrows or labels touching wires join them) or one net split;
- a crossing decided wrongly (dot = connected; hop arc = not connected);
- a wrong component type (NMOS/PMOS/NPN/PNP, single-ended vs fully differential amplifier),
  a missed component, or a detection that is not a component;
- op-amp + and - inputs swapped.

Rules:
- Most of the netlist is probably correct. Only edit what IMAGE 1 shows to be wrong.
- Net names do not matter, only which pins share a net. Do not rename nets.
- Ground and supply symbols are not components.
- If everything is correct, return an empty list.

Return ONLY a JSON object (no markdown fences) of the form
{"edits": [ ... ]}
where each edit is one of the following (you may add a short "why" field to any edit):
{"op": "set_pin", "component": "M3", "pin": "Drain", "net": "net5"}
    Connect one pin to a net. Use an existing net name, or a NEW name (e.g. "new1") to give
    the pin a net of its own / to split a net (give every pin that moves the same new name).
{"op": "swap_pins", "component": "M3", "pins": ["Drain", "Source"]}
    Exchange the nets of two pins of one component (e.g. drain/source, InP/InN, Pos/Neg).
{"op": "merge_nets", "nets": ["net2", "net7"]}
    The listed nets are one net (wires that are actually connected). The first name is kept.
{"op": "change_type", "component": "Q1", "type": "PNP", "pins": {"Collector": "net1", ...}}
    Wrong component type. "pins" is optional when the pins map one-to-one
    (NMOS/PMOS/NPN/PNP: Drain<->Collector, Gate<->Base, Source<->Emitter;
    Res/Cap/Ind; Diode/Current); otherwise give the full pin -> net mapping for the new type.
{"op": "add_component", "type": "Res", "pins": {"Pos": "net1", "Neg": "GND"}}
    A component the pipeline missed.
{"op": "remove_component", "component": "R4"}
    Not a real component (e.g. a detection on text or a symbol that is not a device).
{"op": "remove_pin", "component": "M2", "pin": "Body"}
    Only for the optional MOSFET Body pin.
